Sahel.et: Ultimately from Arabic سَاحِل (sāḥil, “border of the desert”, literally “coast”).

s: Sahel (semi-arid region in northern Africa, bordering the Sahara)

Sahne.et: From Middle High German sāne, from Old French sain, saime, from Latin sagīna (“nourishment”), of uncertain origin. Compare Middle Low German sān, sāne, saeum, from the same Old French source.

s: dollop of cream on a drink
a female given name, variant of Sarah
a type of cream-filled layer cake
